title: Algorithmic Justice and Responsible AI Journalism: A Comparative Communication Policy Perspective in East Asia
authors: Renxiudi Huang; Linjia Bai
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence and automated content curation rapidly reshape the global media landscape, the intersection of algorithmic justice and media governance has become a critical frontier for sustainable development. This study provides a comparative communication policy analysis of China and South Korea, focusing explicitly on how their distinct regulatory toolkits address the tension between algorithmic fairness and platform accountability in AI journalism. While China utilizes a top-down, state-centric regulatory framework emphasizing ideological security, algorithmic registration, and strict synthetic media labeling, South Korea employs a multi-stakeholder co-regulation model driven by personal data protection, anti-monopoly platform intervention, and civil society oversight. Through a detailed textual analysis of key policy documents—including China's Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendations and South Korea's Guidelines for AI Service Ethics to Protect Users—alongside empirical evidence from prominent algorithmic news curation platforms (Toutiao and Naver), this paper evaluates the implementation efficacy and structural trade-offs of each nation's approach. We demonstrate that while both models mitigate the risks of digital infodemics and algorithmic bias, they face contrasting trade-offs between regulatory efficiency and editorial independence. Finally, this study introduces the "Policy-Media-Society" (PMS) responsive governance framework, clarifying how systemic institutional adaptations can advance UN Sustainable Development Goal 16 (SDG 16) by ensuring public access to transparent, verified information.

title: MOVPE growth and characterization of AlPN layers for HFETs
authors: Eberhard Richter; Frank Brunner; S. Hagedorn; Carsten Netzel; Kornelius Tetzner; Abdul Rehman; Robert Martin; M. Weyers
venue: Strathprints: The University of Strathclyde institutional repository (University of Strathclyde)
abstract: The growth of AlPN layers by metalorganic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) and their use as barrier layers on GaN buffer layers for heterojunction field effect transistors (HFETs) was investigated. Quantitative energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), wavelength-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (WDX), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements were used to determine the atomic P content of the AlPN layers. PH3 and tertiarybutyl phosphine (tBP) proved to be very similar P precursors for the MOVPE growth of AlPN layers. The AlPN HFET epitaxial layer structures were characterized by atomic force microscopy (AFM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Hall effect, conductivity, and capacitance–voltage (CV) measurements. AlPN/AlN/GaN/sapphire HFET devices were fabricated and characterized. The results indicate that AlPN, similar to Ga1-xPxN, suffers from a preferential incorporation of P onto the group III lattice site instead of the desired N site, and may therefore not allow for downscaling of HFET devices as predicted for the lattice changes when incorporating P at N sites.

title: Krum-Inspired Central Teacher Selection and Residual Channel Bottlenecks for Efficient DeepSC
authors: Rami Eid; Mostafa Jammoul; Omar Kaaki; Maria Slim; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Deploying transformer-based semantic communication models on edge devices requires compression that preserves semantic fidelity under channel variability. We study a compressed deep semantic communication (DeepSC) student trained by multi-teacher knowledge distillation and combine two ideas: (i) a residual channel bottleneck that splits the transmitted representation into a base stream and a residual stream with unequal power allocation, and (ii) a Krum-inspired, medoid-style centrality criterion that selects a single central teacher from a five-model ensemble, applied at the logit and intermediate-feature levels and combined with a feature-dominant distillation loss. On the EuroParl benchmark, a two-layer student recovers about 98% of the four-layer teacher's bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU)-1 under additive white Gaussian noise, with 93% of its BLEU-4 and 96% of its sentence-BERT (SBERT) score, and about 89%, 77%, and 87% of the teacher's BLEU-1, BLEU-4, and SBERT, respectively, under Rayleigh fading, while reducing non-embedding parameters by 1.33x and single-teacher inference latency by 1.79x (9.0x relative to a five-teacher ensemble used here as an upper-bound reference, not a deployment baseline). Controlled ablations over three seeds indicate complementary contributions of about +8.4% BLEU-1 (+9.6% SBERT) from the residual bottleneck and +3.0% (+2.9% SBERT) from centrality-based selection over mean aggregation. A decoder-mode ablation shows that the base stream alone recovers about two-thirds of the full BLEU-1 while the residual stream alone collapses, supporting the role of the residual as a refinement on top of the base.

title: Where to Defend? Layer-Wise Adversarial Training for Robust Transformer-Based Semantic Communications
authors: Maria Slim; Razane Tajeddine; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC), a Transformer-based encoder-decoder, achieves semantic fidelity over noisy channels but remains vulnerable to adversarial perturbations injected at multiple stages of the pipeline. We present a layer-wise robustness framework that compares fast gradient sign method (FGSM), projected gradient descent (PGD), and l2-normalized fast gradient method (FGM) defenses at the embedding output, and then uses PGD to analyze three attack and defense points: the embedding output, encoder output, and channel-encoder bottleneck. We evaluate reconstruction on Europarl and UK Hansard and sentiment classification on SST2 and YELP under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading. A first-order damage budget, {epsilon} times the l1 norm of the clean-input loss gradient at each injection point, predicts the attack-severity ordering, and the transfer matrix reveals asymmetric defense transfer: the embedding defense transfers strongly to encoder attacks, whereas encoder defenses degrade robustness against upstream attacks. For reconstruction, encoder-point training yields the largest matched gain but fails severely under embedding attacks; joint embedding-plus-encoder training retains comparable gains under encoder attacks while mitigating this mismatch failure, and Rayleigh fading attenuates robustness gains and degradation. For classification, three of four defenses collapse to constant predictors; only the channel-encoder defense remains non-degenerate, suggesting a protective role for the 128D-to-16D bottleneck. At a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 9 dB and perturbation budget {epsilon} = 0.3, the matched encoder defense recovers bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) from ~ 0.10 to ~ 0.64 on Europarl/AWGN, whereas the mismatched encoder defense yields a -0.444 BLEU change relative to the undefended baseline under an embedding attack.

title: Semantic-Aware Sub-Band Allocation for Terahertz Communications
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: This paper studies semantic-aware sub-band al- location for terahertz (THz) communication systems, where frequency-selective molecular absorption creates highly non- uniform sub-band qualities. Unlike conventional formulations, semantic fidelity depends nonlinearly on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and is also sentence-specific, leading to a non-separable assignment problem that is generally not solvable using simple ordering-based policies. To address this, we use a sentence-BERT (SBERT)-based surrogate model that predicts semantic fidelity from the sentence embedding and sub-band SNR. We propose an importance-aware scheduler that assigns sentences to sub- bands based on their semantic contribution using an oracle utility function that captures importance-weighted semantic similarity across sentence-sub-band pairs. A neural scheduler is then trained through imitation learning to approximate the oracle policy at more than 200x lower runtime than full DeepSC- based oracle evaluation. Integrated with a deep-learning-enabled semantic communication (DeepSC) system, the proposed method consistently outperforms all benchmark schemes and approaches oracle-level performance under realistic THz channel conditions.

title: Flexible Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding: A Vibrotactile Example
authors: Shuijie Li; Kemi Chen; Runjie Wang; Tiesong Zhao; Xiaoming Tao
abstract: The increasing demand for real-time tactile communication in multimedia systems has exposed the limitations of existing Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) techniques. While current JSCC models facilitate end-to-end optimization, they typically operate at fixed coding rates and require separate model instances for different rate settings. This results in significant storage overhead and limited adaptability to dynamic bandwidth conditions. To address these challenges, we propose the Flexible Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding (FD-JSCC) framework for vibrotactile signals, which supports flexible-rate transmission without the need for model switching. The FD-JSCC integrates a flexible-rate encoder-decoder enhanced with Hierarchical Gain Adaptation Module (HGAM) and Rate-Switchable Residual Module (RSRM), enabling bitrate-aware compression by selectively preserving salient vibrotactile features. Additionally, we introduce a Channel Feature Processing Module (CFPM), which leverages real-time SNR information to enhance robustness against channel noise and signal degradation. Trained on the IEEE 1918.1.1 vibrotactile dataset, FD-JSCC achieves reconstruction performance comparable to fixed-rate baselines (e.g., DeepSC-S), while reducing storage requirements by 61.1\% when supporting four rates. These results underscore its potential for scalable, low-latency tactile communication in next-generation networks.

title: Compressibility is not Feedback: A Random-access Gap in Causal Semantic Repair
authors: Milad Bafarassat
abstract: Semantic feedback can repair a noisy first decode without retransmitting the whole message, but current end-to-end evaluations hide where a feedback design fails. An oracle that sees both the source-side state and receiver observation may describe a useful correction with few bits, while the receiver, which sees only its own observation, may not know which correction to request. We formulate these as distinct direct and receiver-constrained coding problems, connect repair distortion to retained local utility and prove a random-access separation: one direct bit is exact although receiver utility vanishes with the number of source-conditioned alternatives. A synthetic ladder verifies the exact law. In paired populations of eight Reuters text-JSCC codecs, the trained recurrent population retains over three times more direct 16-bit repair value than the trained DeepSC population despite comparable full-repair opportunity. Nevertheless, an entropy-valid receiver audit across all eight recurrent checkpoints does not resolve against repetition, source-only or shuffled-index controls. The results show that compressible repair is an upper bound, not evidence of deployable feedback, and motivate reporting both rate curves under matched resources.

title: SignDeepSC: A Semantic Signature-based Approach for Robust Semantic Communication
authors: Khalil Alhaj; Razane Tajeddine; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Semantic communication systems such as deep semantic communication (DeepSC) offer high efficiency but are vulnerable to adversarial attacks on their underlying neural networks. We address a physical-layer man-in-the-middle (MitM) threat in which an adversary injects perturbations into the transmitted signal to distort its meaning. We propose SignDeepSC, an architectural defense that achieves adversarial robustness without requiring explicit adversarial example generation during training. The approach is built on a perceiver-inspired semantic signature, a compact vector summary of the source features transmitted over a separate low-rate auxiliary channel. This signature is used by a self-repairing decoder that leverages cross-attention to correct distortions and can additionally drive a scrambler that shuffles the feature layout. We evaluate SignDeepSC over Rayleigh fading and additive white Gaussian noise channels under both single-step fast gradient sign method (FGSM) and iterative projected gradient descent (PGD) attacks. Under PGD ($ε= 0.7$), at 12~dB signal-to-noise ratio with Rayleigh fading, SignDeepSC achieves a bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU-4) score of 0.237 and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) sentence similarity of 0.646, outperforming all baselines without degrading clean-channel performance, when the signature channel is well protected.

title: Structured Spectral Compression based Low-Bitrate Secure Speech Communications for Internet of Things assisted Non-Terrestrial Networks
authors: Li Ping Qian; Zhehan Chen; Qianru Wang; Qian Wang; Yuan Wu; Xuemin Sherman Shen
abstract: This paper focuses on the Low-Bitrate Secure Speech Communications based on the Structured Spectral Compression (LB-S2C2). Specifically, the Mel spectral matrix of the speech signal is first encoded at the transmitter side through compressive sensing based on waveform segmentation and data quantization. Then, the Automatic Repeat Request (ARQ) is combined with forward error correction to achieve reliable transmission of speech signals over wireless channels. Thirdly, the received signals are recovered as the speech at the receiver side. Finally, we conduct a series of simulation experiments for the performance evaluation of LB-S2C2. Our simulations reveal that the dictionary matrix used for the speech reconstruction is different from the one used for the high-order matrix sparsification by even only approximately 0.1%, and then the accurate speech recovery fails. It implies that the speech data can be securely transmitted when the dictionary matrix is preserved. More importantly, the LB-S2C2 exhibits a very high privacy protection capability with the average voiceprint similarity to be only 0.3, which is much lower than the 0.8 of the semantic speech communication scheme DeepSC-S, and even lower than the 0.33 of the latest speech communication scheme OFI-OFCNB. In addition, our simulations reveal that the proposed structured speech coding boasts a time complexity of merely O(n), and the proposed speech recovery scheme requires the 12-bit memory storage only, which outperforms the traditional encryption algorithms proposed for speech communications. In comparison with the conventional compression techniques, our spectral compression method renders the coding rate of only 3.9kbps, which is lower than the current lowest speech coding rate of 6.3kbps achieved by G.723.

title: Semantic Communications in the THz Band
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: Semantic and terahertz (THz)-band communications are algorithmic and spectral enablers of future wireless networks. This work investigates deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC) over THz channels. We show that DeepSC models trained solely under additive white Gaussian noise generalize well to the tested THz block- and fast-fading channels when receiver-side compensation is applied. To enable fully data-driven reception, we propose a lightweight neural detector that does not require channel state information (CSI). At 0.3 THz, DeepSC outperforms a throughput-matched traditional coded communication system baseline over 0-12 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), achieving more than 50 percentage-point higher Bilingual Evaluation Understudy unigram (BLEU-1) score. The proposed pilot-free detector outperforms minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalization with both perfect and imperfect CSI and remains robust to frequency offsets up to 50 MHz, highlighting the resilience of semantic communication to THz channel impairments.

title: Image Semantic Communication with Quadtree Partition-based Coding
authors: Yinhuan Huang; Zhijin Qin
abstract: Deep learning based semantic communication (DeepSC) system has emerged as a promising paradigm for efficient wireless transmission. However, existing image DeepSC methods, frequently encounter challenges in balancing rate-distortion performance and computational complexity, and often exhibit inferior performance compared to traditional schemes, especially on high-resolution datasets. To address these limitations, we propose a novel image DeepSC system, using quadtree partition-based joint semantic-channel coding, named Quad-DeepSC, which maintains low complexity while achieving state-of-the-art transmission performance. Based on maturing learned image compression technologies, we establish a unified DeepSC system design and training pipeline. The proposed Quad-DeepSC integrates quadtree partition-based entropy estimation and feature coding modules with lightweight feature extraction and reconstruction networks to form an end-to-end architecture. During training, all components except the feature coding modules are jointly optimized as a compact learned image codec, Quad-LIC, for source compression tasks. The pretrained Quad-LIC is then embedded into Quad-DeepSC and fine-tuned end-to-end over wireless channels. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Quad-DeepSC is the first DeepSC system to surpass conventional communication systems, which employ VTM for source coding and adopt the optimal MCS index under 3GPP standards for channel coding and digital modulation, in performance across datasets of varying resolutions. Notably, both Quad-DeepSC and Quad-LIC exhibit minimal latency, rendering them well-suited for deployment in real-time wireless communication systems.

title: VQ-VAE Based Digital Semantic Communication with Importance-Aware OFDM Transmission
authors: Ming Lyu; Hao Chen; Dan Wang; Chen Qiu; Guangyin Feng; Nan Ma; Xiaodong Xu
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) significantly reduces redundant data and improves transmission efficiency by extracting the latent features of information. However, most of the conventional deep learning-based SemCom systems focus on analog transmission and lack in compatibility with practical digital communications. This paper proposes a vector quantized-variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) based digital SemCom system that directly transmits the semantic features and incorporates the importance-aware orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) transmission to enhance the SemCom performance, where the VQ-VAE generates a discrete codebook shared between the transmitter and receiver. At transmitter, the latent semantic features are firstly extracted by VQ-VAE, and then the shared codebook is adopted to match these features, which are subsequently transformed into a discrete version to adapt the digital transmission. To protect the semantic information, an importance-aware OFDM transmission strategy is proposed to allocate the key features near the OFDM reference signals, where the feature importance is derived from the gradient-based method. At the receiver, the features are rematched with the shared codebook to further correct errors. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms the conventional DeepSC and achieves better reconstruction performance under low SNR region.

title: AI-ENABLED SEMANTIC COMMUNICATION ARCHITECTURE FOR 6G NETWORKS: AN INTELLIGENT, CONTEXT-AWARE AND RESOURCE-EFFICIENT FRAMEWORK WITH HYBRID OPTIMIZATION
authors: Ganesan S.; Jagatheeshkumar G.
venue: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
abstract: Communication architectures that can enable intelligent services, vast connectivity, ultra-low latency, and extremely heterogeneous applications are necessary due to the sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks' rapid expansion. Large amounts of redundant data are communicated with significant bandwidth, energy, and computational overhead since conventional communication systems are primarily concerned with correct bit-level transmission. By conveying task-relevant meaning rather than full raw data, semantic communication overcomes this constraint. This research presents an AI-Enabled Semantic Communication Architecture for 6G Networks that combines context-aware decision-making, intelligent semantic extraction, and hybrid optimization. Gray Wolf Optimization (GWO) optimizes transmission parameters and semantic reconstruction quality, whereas Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) selects semantic features and allocates communication resources in the suggested framework. The optimization method is dynamically modified by a context-aware semantic controller based on network resources, channel conditions, and application needs. The framework is intended to maximize semantic similarity and communication efficiency while minimizing semantic distortion, latency, energy usage, and bandwidth utilization. Text-based semantic communication is used in an experimental assessment framework with different network loads and signal-to-noise ratios. For upcoming 6G applications, the suggested architecture offers a basis for resource-efficient, flexible, and intelligent semantic communication.

title: Multi-Source and Multi-Dimensional Information Fusion in Resource-Constrained Edge Networks
authors: Yushi Wang; Zhengxin Yu; Guhan Zheng; Wang Miao; Merouane Abdelkader Debbah
abstract: Multi-source semantic information fusion enables edge networks to support global inference using observations collected by distributed terminals. However, limited communication and computation resources restrict semantic uploading, leaving the edge server with incomplete tokens that differ in modality, semantic granularity, arrival time, and channel condition. The value of these tokens also depends on the complementary or redundant information provided by other terminals. In this paper, we propose a multi-source and multi-dimensional semantic information fusion framework that coordinates terminal uploading and edge-side fusion under resource constraints. We develop Hyper-Slot to combine semantic content with available token attributes through iterative token-to-slot assignment and slot-to-token feedback, producing a compact representation for global inference. To encourage useful semantic uploading, we further design a contribution-based incentive mechanism that uses Hyper-Slot assignments to evaluate information coverage and cross-type complementarity. A bi-level Stackelberg-Nash game determines the server reward pool and terminal transmission-quality strategies while accounting for computation and communication energy costs. Experiments on a tri-modal extension of COCO2014 and image-text retrieval on Flickr30K show that Hyper-Slot improves mAP by 3.66 percentage points and RSum by 15.9 points over the strongest evaluated baselines, respectively, while reducing the number of parameters by more than 80% compared with a naive concatenation-based fusion baseline.

title: Adaptive Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication with Pretrained Semantic Encoding and Effectiveness-Aware Equalization for Beyond-5G/6G Networks
authors: Haseeb Ur Rehman; Kashif Bashir; Afzal Shah Muhammad; Suleman Soomro Muhammad; Umar Shahzad Khan Muhammad; Nouman Bashir
abstract: Semantic communication seeks to transmit task-relevant meaning rather than reproduce every source bit, but learned semantic representations can deteriorate sharply when they are perturbed by channel noise. This paper presents an adaptive, goal-oriented semantic communication framework that combines a pretrained Sentence-BERT (SBERT) encoder with a noise-conditioned neural equalizer. Text is mapped to a 384-dimensional semantic vector, perturbed by additive white Gaussian noise, and processed by the equalizer only when the estimated noise standard deviation exceeds an activation threshold of τ=0.05. A cosine-similarity rule then determines whether the recovered representation is accepted or sent for refinement or retransmission. In the reported embedding-domain experiments, adaptive equalization increased mean semantic similarity from 0.2475 to 0.6303 at σ=0.20 and from 0.0740 to 0.3545 at σ=0.70. The corresponding absolute gains were 0.3828 and 0.2805, respectively. At σ≤0.05, the equalizer was bypassed and produced no measurable change, avoiding unnecessary correction under mild perturbations. These results establish a proof of concept for noise-triggered recovery of pretrained semantic embeddings.

title: Language Model-Aided Text Semantic Communications for Digital-Twin Interaction
authors: Bo Chen; Can Wang; Chen Xu; Shuai Zhang; Huachun Tan; Liting Zhang
abstract: Reliable semantic interaction between physical entities and their virtual counterparts is fundamental to digital-twin operation. In challenging wireless environments, however, channel noise and fading corrupt continuous semantic representations, causing semantic drift, token substitutions, repetitive generation, and premature termination at the receiver. This article proposes LM-DeepSC, a language model-aided text semantic communication framework for digital twins. The framework combines end-to-end joint source–channel semantic transmission with a trainable continuous semantic feature adapter at the receiver. The adapter projects channel-corrupted features produced by the semantic decoder into continuous conditioning representations that a frozen pretrained language model can directly exploit. Consequently, the receiver jointly exploits residual communication evidence, contextual dependencies, and pretrained linguistic knowledge to reconstruct the source text without first committing to an error-prone intermediate token sequence. Experiments over additive white Gaussian noise and Rayleigh fading channels show that LM-DeepSC consistently outperforms DeepSC in multi-order BLEU scores and sentence similarity under the same transmitted channel-symbol budget. Evaluations over ten independent AWGN channel realizations further demonstrate a relative reduction of 46.3–71.0% in token substitution rate. On MASSIVE control instructions unseen during communication-model training, LM-DeepSC improves downstream intent-classification accuracy by 6.3–15.5 percentage points over DeepSC. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed LM-assisted receiver for robust text interaction under noisy wireless channels, with potential application to digital-twin systems.

title: Predictive Semantic-Aware Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request for Reliable and Efficient 6G Communications
authors: Osman KAYA; Muhammet Ali Karabulut; Can Eyüpoğlu; Oktay Karakuş
abstract: Hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) remains the backbone of link-layer reliability, yet it was designed for a setting in which every bit matters equally and the channel of the next slot is unknown. Neither assumption holds in semantic communication over time-varying channels: some parts of a message are decisive for the receiver’s task while others are not, and the deep fade that destroyed a first transmission is usually still present when an immediate retransmission arrives. This article proposes predictive semantic-aware HARQ (PSA-HARQ), a retransmission framework that makes its decisions at the level of individual semantic units and bases them jointly on how much each unit matters and on how the channel is expected to evolve. Semantic importance is extracted from a Transformer semantic encoder, a lightweight recurrent predictor forecasts the channel a few slots ahead, and a finite-horizon optimal-stopping controller decides, for every unit and every slot, whether to transmit, wait for a better slot, or abandon the unit. The forecast enters the controller through a confidence-weighted estimator whose weight is tracked at run time from the observed prediction errors, so that the policy falls back to the statistics-only optimum whenever the predictor becomes uninformative. Simulations over a vehicular situational-awareness task and over a real public record-classification dataset, with finite-blocklength coding and time-correlated Rayleigh fading, show that PSA-HARQ matches or exceeds the task accuracy of conventional HARQ in the low-SNR regime where retransmissions are most frequent, while transmitting far fewer blocks and consuming far less energy at the same channel condition. A cost-matched ablation shows that semantic importance and channel prediction contribute complementary gains. The results indicate that anticipating the channel, rather than merely reacting to it, is a practical and largely untapped lever for reliable and efficient 6G semantic communication.

title: A2SSC: An Agent-based Adaptive Semantic Speech Communication System
authors: Dongxu Yang; Fangyu Liu; Peiwen Jiang; Li Xiao; Shi Jin
abstract: Abstract In wireless environments with weak coverage or rapidly changing channels, reliable speech transmission is challenging due to fluctuating channel quality and limited bandwidth. Semantic communication offers a promising solution by focusing on the transmission of essential information rather than raw signals. Although existing semantic speech communication systems have made progress, they still lack decision mechanisms that are aware of both content and channel, limiting their robustness and flexibility. In this paper, we propose an agent-based adaptive semantic speech communication system (A2SSC). The system encodes textual content and speaker characteristics separately, and adaptively allocates transmission resources based on the importance of the speech content and the current channel conditions. At the same time, we incorporate an agent-based architecture to ensure system flexibility and scalability, and introduce an online learning mechanism that allows the system to continuously adapt to changing channel conditions after deployment. Experimental results show that A2SSC achieves comparable word error rate (WER) and speaker similarity (SS) to state-of-the-art baselines, while reducing the maximum num-ber of transmitted symbols by 62.5%. Moreover, the system maintains robust performance across varying channel conditions, demonstrating its effectiveness for reliable and efficient speech transmission in challenging wireless environments.

title: Machine-Learned Mismatch and Task Preservation Beliefs in CoSMA DAI for Common Knowledge Aware Semantic Alignment
authors: Iacovos I. Ioannou; Chrıstophoros Christophorou; Marios Raspopoulos; Vasos Vassiliou
abstract: Correct packet delivery does not guarantee correct semantic interpretation when endpoint meanings for the same learned codeword diverge. CoSMA DAI is proposed for mismatch detection, protected confirmation, task preservation and semantic repair. Channel-conditioned global evidence, semantic class local evidence, temporal dynamics, channel context and protected probe evidence are fused by a causal machine-learned mismatch belief. A transmitter-derived task belief preserves the downstream decision while repair is pending and BDIx agents select guarded intentions for probing, fallback and resynchronisation. Evaluation uses 30 held-out drift seeds, 300 matched null streams and 300 degrading channel controls. Six referenced sequential monitors receive the same conditioned payload score. CoSMA DAI obtains 100.00 percent balanced accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and Matthews correlation coefficient with zero observed matched null false alarms. Its aggregate delay is 5.62 slots, compared with 11.58 slots for the other zero false alarm method. The task-preservation belief maintains 94.73 percent task accuracy through every divergence scenario, above the quantised accuracy ceiling of 0.919 of the semantic path, because it is derived from the unquantised transmitter latent. A task-label-only control confirms that this accuracy is secured by the preservation belief alone, independently of the detector, so task preservation and mismatch detection are decoupled by design and detectors are compared on residual functional semantic outage, outage duration and semantic reconstruction fidelity, which measure the restoration of the semantic representation itself. Without repair, the residual semantic outage is 73.69 percent at 15.97 dB reconstruction fidelity, whereas CoSMA DAI reduces it to 0.73 percent over 6.62 slots at 21.74 dB. Under five declared parity tiers, in which multivariate and supervised baselines receive the identical features, training seeds, protected probe and candidate budget, the protected confirmation stage reduces false repair for every detector to which it is attached. Zero-shot evaluation over 7 unseen mismatch families and 5 unseen link models retains full detection with zero observed false repair in 6 of the 7 families and on every link and identifies receiver-side decoder drift as a condition the present observation model cannot detect. The learned belief is validated at slot level with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.99997 and a class overlap of 0.00039, leave-one-mechanism-out and cross-channel retraining are reported, behaviour is characterised down to the practical detection boundary and scaling to 64-dimensional representations with 2048-entry codebooks is demonstrated. The task-belief mechanism is shown to be economical only for small closed-set output spaces and the channel-conditioning tables are shown to reduce to 6 cells without loss. Every comparator is additionally retuned on the same development budget, paired bootstrap intervals and signed-rank tests are reported over the shared streams, auxiliary traffic and radio energy are normalised per correct decision, authentication of the task belief is specified and charged and transfer to MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 is demonstrated without retraining, including on a convolutional VQ-VAE representation with a jointly learned 512-entry codebook, where foreground segmentation and localisation are restored to within the quantisation limit while a class decision cannot serve either task. The control traffic share is 23.59 percent, which is 12.62 percent lower than the monitor value. The additional semantic side information increases radio energy to 0.393 mJ per stream and reduces control-adjusted resource efficiency to 6.203 source-equivalent bits per channel use. The results therefore establish reliable detection and semantic repair within the principal comparison, with comparator-specific delay advantages and without claiming task-accuracy, semantic-rate or energy superiority.

title: Channel-adaptive semantic token transmission for multimodal edge perception over wireless uplinks
authors: Yong Liao; Zhiyuan Zhu; Dapeng Wu; Ruyan Wang

title: Beyond Task Relevance: Interaction-Aware Semantic Communication for Wireless Agent Collaboration
authors: Yiru Wang; Pengxin Guan; Xiumei Deng; Zehui Xiong
abstract: Semantic communication in multi-agent systems often assumes that task-relevant information benefits the team once delivered. Yet semantic sharing can alter the receiver's decision and increase inter-agent dependence, potentially reducing team utility. Motivated by this phenomenon, we develop an interaction-aware framework for wireless collaboration between heterogeneous agents. We analytically relate communication-induced dependence to expected best-of-team utility and define a team-level semantic value for candidate messages. We consider semantic units at different abstraction levels and formulate a deadline- and power-constrained problem that maximizes predicted team-level net surplus. We derive an interaction-aware policy that selects at most one unit and its transmit power, or chooses not to transmit. Experiments on two verifier-scored optimization tasks show that full-solution exchange induces stronger structural convergence and more adverse team-level effects, whereas method hints exhibit pronounced directionality. Across the evaluated power budgets, our policy achieves the highest net team-level surplus while consuming less energy than semantic-aware and full-solution baselines.

title: Towards High Semantic Fidelity: Hyperdimensional Symbolic Messages in Multi-Agent Communication
authors: Shoucheng Song; Chang Yao; Hao Wu; Youfang Lin; Sheng Han; Kai Lv
abstract: Semantic fidelity is essential for multi-agent communication under non-ideal channels, comprising transmission fidelity and conversion fidelity. Yet existing numerical and neural message formats cannot simultaneously achieve both. To address this, we propose a novel message format-\textbf{H}yperdimensional \textbf{S}ymbolic \textbf{M}essages (HSM) and its corresponding communication framework \textbf{Herm}. For transmission fidelity, Herm suppresses semantic entanglement via an entity-attribute-value structured encoding pipeline. For conversion fidelity, Herm first leverages a receiver-centric ego-binding mechanism to align semantics. Then, a similarity-aware dual-branch fusion module is proposed to prevent critical semantic dilution. To realize explicit message-semantic conversion, we devise an iterative decoding scheme via algebraic inverse operations. Experiments exhibit that Herm outperforms baselines across various noisy scenarios while maintaining superior structural readability.

title: Cryptographically Secure Agent-to-Agent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Karol Budzyn; Adrian Brodzik; Mateusz Szczepkowski
abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) comprise AI agents that collaborate or compete to perform complex, distributed tasks. Their dynamic interactions create opportunities for threat actors to target and impersonate other agents, intercept messages, inject malicious prompts, and exfiltrate sensitive data while simultaneously complicating the detection of anomalous behavior through conventional monitoring. This paper surveys threats and cryptographic challenges in agent-to-agent communication and presents a zero-trust architecture integrating identity, transport security, message integrity, and monitoring. The architecture establishes agent identities via decentralized identifiers and task-scoped verifiable credentials backed by a permissioned ledger, enforcing least-privilege authorization. For transport security, it provides mutually authenticated, crypto-agile TLS with hybrid post-quantum key establishment, and evaluates KEMTLS with pre-distributed public keys to reduce handshake overhead. Signed CBOR envelopes preserve payload integrity across multi-hop exchanges, while zero-knowledge proofs verify declared task constraints without exposing underlying inputs. Context-aware monitoring of inter-agent messages, tool activity, and execution telemetry informs the setting of risk-based trust thresholds and supports the detection of behavioral anomalies. Together, these mechanisms provide an integrated framework for securing and auditing agent communication, with implications for other agentic protocols and prospective 6G semantic communication.

title: LLM-Guided Dual-Stage Latency Optimization for Closed-Loop 6G V2I Digital Twins
authors: Liu Cao; Peide Li; Yuan Yang; Zhaoyu Liu; Lyutianyang Zhang; Jinke Ren; Shuguang Cui
abstract: Wireless Digital Twins are emerging as a key enabler for predictive network control in 6G Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) systems. However, closed-loop V2I DTs face two dual-stage communication bottlenecks arising from model parameter exchange for V2I DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic delivery after each reconstruction. This paper proposes a closed-loop dual-stage End-to-End (E2E) latency optimization framework that integrates Compressed Personalized Federated Learning with a unified Large-Language-Model-guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approach. A CPFL-enabled decision-oriented V2I DT is first constructed by jointly predicting Path Loss (PL) and Quality-of-Experience (QoE)-oriented Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Then the framework comprises two temporally coupled but latency-wise distinct optimization stages: Stage I minimizes the joint Uplink (UL) and Downlink (DL) E2E transmission latency of compressed shared backbone's parameters, and Stage II minimizes the service-aware E2E latency of multi-service V2I traffic. As the two stages share aligned agent roles and action space, we develop a unified Semantic-Aware Guidance-Enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization framework, in which the LLM acts as a training-time semantic planner that provides high-level traffic splitting and power allocation guidance to reduce inefficient exploration, while the MARL agents execute feasible low-level actions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables efficient V2I DT reconstruction and significantly reduces both E2E latency for DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic. The proposed SAGE-MAPPO supports cross-stage policy reuse by sequentially solving the two stages within each DT update cycle, which accelerates convergence relative to the existing baselines and facilitates timely DT updates in dynamic V2I scenarios.

title: DialFork: Going Beyond Factuality to Evaluate Procedural Hallucination in Conversational Agents
authors: Sergio Burdisso; Esaú Villatoro-Tello; Dairazalia Sánchez-Cortés; Yanis Labrak; Jordi Luque; Milos Cernak; Petr Motlicek
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deployed as conversational agents are increasingly expected to follow procedural logic. While factual hallucination has received extensive attention, a different failure mode has been overlooked: procedural hallucination, in which an agent produces individually fluent and factually plausible utterances while deviating from the intended conversational process. We introduce DialFork, the first benchmark to measure this failure mode on raw dialogue text. DialFork is built by forking conformant dialogues at controlled turn positions and injecting one of four hallucination types, yielding 36,278 dialogues across 24 tasks in 12 domains; 30 human annotators validate the construction. We define three evaluation tasks that characterize procedural deviation at three granularities: how far a set of dialogues deviates from conformant ones (monitoring deployed agents), how far a single dialogue does (procedural retrieval), and at which turn a dialogue first goes off-track (real-time guardrails). For the first two, we propose dialog-flow-aware metrics, FlowKL and FlowScore, that compare dialogues by how they unfold rather than their content. At the dialogue level, FlowScore significantly outperforms all baselines across seven encoders, showing that semantic similarity is no substitute for procedural similarity. We release DialFork under open licenses at https://github.com/idiap/dialfork, hoping the community will measure conversational process alongside content.

title: Mobility-Budget-Constrained Submodular Maximization for Distributed Semantic Multi-Robot Exploration
authors: Changxuan Yao; Sandilya Sai Garimella; Lu Gan; Panagiotis Tsiotras
abstract: Multi-robot exploration under communication and mobility constraints requires balancing information gain with reachability. We present a distributed semantic exploration framework that combines Dirichlet mapping, budget-constrained trajectory selection, and Resource-Aware distributed Greedy (RAG) coordination. Each robot clusters frontiers, computes terrain- and heading-aware least-cost paths with a single budget-limited Dijkstra search, and selects feasible paths by marginal information gain, represented by the expected reduction in Dirichlet entropy. Each robot's per-round selection is exact, the team's joint per-round information gain is at least half the centralized optimum, and the bound degrades gracefully under limited communication. Ten-run gridworld ablations show improved coverage, semantic mIoU, and map certainty with lower entropy and traversal cost per unit distance than shortest-distance frontier selection. Budget-sensitivity experiments show that an intermediate budget best balances path reach and receding-horizon execution. In photorealistic full-system simulation against five coordination rules run in their native published forms, the proposed method attains the highest mean coverage and semantic accuracy while being the only one that respects the per-trajectory mobility budget.

title: LURE: a Phase-Labelled Synthetic Corpus of Online-Grooming Exchanges
authors: Emanuele Florindi; Valentina Franzoni; Ludovico Guercio; Alfredo Milani; Mattia Polticchia
abstract: Phase-annotated conversational data is essential for studying the progression of online grooming of minors and for developing early warning tools. However, the only publicly available source (i.e., Perverted-Justice archive, which contains a subset coded using ChatCoder) is small, outdated, and frozen. We present a synthetic corpus of groomer-victim exchanges, generated using a retrieval-augmented pipeline running on institutional hardware. This pipeline uses an openly available, eight-billion-parameter, refusal-ablated language model. The corpus was created using the five stages of the responsible-generation protocol for synthetic datasets: ontology-driven design based on the ChatCoder luring-communication scheme (eight communicative tags mapped onto four grooming phases); multi-model prompt testing; human-in-the-loop supervision; semantic and feature-level validation; and modality-aware documentation. The released corpus contains 2,121 unique exchanges across seven tags and four phases, each accompanied by a Plutchik emotion field. Validation quantifies the integrity and lexical profile of the corpus, as well as the reproduction of real seed lines, in-domain label recoverability (tag accuracy: 0.85; phase accuracy: 0.93) and its transfer to real ChatCoder offender lines, which were coded automatically at the eight-tag level (31,640 lines) and by human coders at the three-construct level (10,876 posts). Accuracy was measured for lexical and sentence-embedding features, while a real-versus-synthetic discriminator was able to separate the two domains with 91% accuracy. The scope of the corpus includes controlled, phase-conditioned experimentation, pipeline development and augmentation alongside real data and awareness material. The corpus, its datasheet and the audit code are released with vetted access.

title: Factors Affecting a Curriculum Based on Citizenship Legal Literacy Education
authors: Kobra Gholizadeh Chennab; Shahram Ranjdoust
venue: International Journal of Education and Cognitive Sciences
abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to identify the factors affecting a curriculum based on citizenship legal literacy education in order to improve the quality of civic education in Iran’s educational system. Methods and Materials: This applied and developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, the statistical population included experts in education, curriculum planning, social sciences, and citizenship rights. Participants were selected through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were collected through 15 semi-structured interviews, which continued until theoretical saturation was achieved. The qualitative data were analyzed using MaxQDA software through open, axial, and selective coding. The extracted themes were then organized to develop a conceptual structure for a curriculum based on citizenship legal literacy education. Findings: The inferential findings supported a multidimensional structure for citizenship legal literacy education. The analysis indicated that five key components formed the core of the proposed curriculum model: citizenship rights education, values and beliefs, practical empowerment, development of social interaction, and media and digital literacy education. These components represented interrelated knowledge-based, attitudinal, behavioral, and social indicators. The findings showed that emphasis on citizens’ rights and responsibilities, justice-oriented attitudes, dialogue skills, social participation, legal awareness, responsible media use, and digital literacy plays a decisive role in designing an effective curriculum for educating law-abiding and participatory citizens. Conclusion: The results suggest that citizenship legal literacy education in Iran requires a shift from the mere transmission of theoretical concepts toward a competency-based, participatory, and practice-oriented curriculum. Such a curriculum can contribute to strengthening civic awareness, promoting legal responsibility, enhancing social participation, supporting educational justice, and preparing students for active and responsible citizenship in contemporary society.

title: Designing an Educational Planning Model Based on the Agricultural Value Chain with a Qualitative Approach
authors: Bentolhoda Ramezanzadeh; Hamidreza Arasteh; Kamran Mohammadkhani; Abbasali Motalebi
venue: Future of Work and Digital Management Journal
abstract: Educational planning based on the agricultural value chain, as a comprehensive and systematic approach, can make a substantial contribution to improving quality and productivity in the agricultural sector. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to design an educational planning model based on the agricultural value chain in citrus orchards in northern Iran. This study is classified as qualitative grounded-theory research. The statistical population consisted of 20 experts and faculty members of the Agricultural Research, Education and Extension Organization. Interviews were used for data collection, and MAXQDA 2020 software was employed for data analysis. The findings identified the research components, including causal conditions consisting of core content, educational activities, and supplementary programs; the central phenomenon, namely educational programs based on the agricultural value chain; contextual factors including macro-level policies and culture; intervening factors including evaluation, core policies, competition, and educational approaches; strategies including organizational strategies and environmental strategies; and outcomes including optimal value chain management, quality orientation, and educational enhancement.

title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis of Fashion and Apparel Related Reviews using Transformer Model
authors: Foud Ameri; Ghasem Bakhshandeh; Maryam Darvishi
venue: Journal of Management and Business Solutions
abstract: The increasing reliance on e-commerce has led to a surge in customer-generated content, making sentiment analysis a crucial tool for understanding consumer preferences. This study presents a novel aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) approach to extract fine-grained insights from customer reviews across multiple product categories, including lingerie, women’s clothing, men’s clothing, kids’ apparel, home & furniture, and flowers & plants. We employ exploratory data analysis (EDA) to uncover key patterns in customer sentiment and utilize a transformer-based model with contrastive learning to enhance sentiment classification accuracy. Our approach effectively captures sentiment variations across nine different aspects, including quality, value for money, style, fit, material, warmth, comfort, support, and how well the product fits. The results demonstrate that our model outperforms traditional sentiment analysis methods, offering a more structured understanding of customer feedback. By analyzing customer sentiments from reviews, businesses can identify dissatisfaction patterns that may contribute to customer churn. Addressing these issues proactively can help improve customer retention and loyalty. These insights can help businesses refine their product offerings and improve customer satisfaction across diverse e-commerce categories.

title: Bio-Inspired Auditory Processing: Coupling Parallel Resonate-and-Fire Dynamics with Ternary Recurrent Networks for Speech Recognition
authors: Pavlos Poulos; Katelyn Sadorf; Themos Stafylakis; Costas A. Anastassiou
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise energy-efficient inference through sparse, event-driven computation, yet remain constrained on continuous, context-dependent tasks such as automatic speech recognition (ASR). A key bottleneck is the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron, whose membrane decay erases information across pauses and phonetic boundaries while it must both extract features and retain long-range context. Inspired by cortical separation of nonlinear filtering and somatic integration, we introduce the Spiking Ternary GRU (stGRU): a ternary-weight gated recurrent unit performs temporal filtering, while downstream Resonate-and-Fire (RF) neurons generate the binary spike stream driving the next block's event pathway. This makes binary event transmission a native training constraint rather than a separate deployment-time activation quantization step; together with ternary weights, learned projections avoid dense floating-point matrix MACs. Trained end-to-end on LibriSpeech-960, Small, Medium, and Large stGRUs reach 8.09%, 7.04%, and $6.44 \pm 0.17\%$ WER on test-clean without an external language model. To our knowledge, these are the first matrix-MAC-free spiking networks without a learned ANN sequence decoder to achieve single-digit WER on LibriSpeech. The architecture also achieves 10.88% test CER on Aishell-1 (9.28% on dev) when trained from scratch. Internally, trained networks develop a depth-graded hierarchy: shallow layers act as fast acoustic filters, while deep layers form slower semantic integrators whose latent representations segregate into part-of-speech manifolds and word-level spike events. Deep-layer firing rates follow lognormal distributions with a sparsity gradient, mirroring hierarchical processing observed in human cortex in vivo. Our biologically grounded architecture combines competitive ASR with favorable modeled compute and memory cost.

title: Joint Semantic-Channel Coding and Modulation for Generative Image Transmission
authors: Hao Cao; Jingkai Ying; Yinhuan Huang; Zhijin Qin; Yuan Shen
abstract: Digital image transmission typically optimizes source coding, channel coding, and modulation separately, limiting how source representations adapt to channel impairments. We propose SemQAM, a joint semantic-channel coding and modulation scheme for generative image transmission converting source to modulated symbols, such as standard QAM symbols. Channel impairments create two challenges: they can corrupt the latent representation at the receiver, and this corruption can compound through autoregressive coding, degrading reconstruction quality. First, SemQAM represents latent features with vector quantization (VQ), maps each VQ index to a QAM symbol, and updates the codeword corresponding to the detected symbol so that channel impairments directly affect codebook learning. Moreover, SemQAM uses the conditional expectation of received codewords to approximate the receiver reconstruction and reduce error propagation during autoregressive coding. SemQAM supports multiple SNRs and CBRs in a unified model, while also supporting conventional source coding through SemQAM-C. Experiments show that (i) under the same LDPC and QAM settings, SemQAM-C outperforms OneDC in LPIPS and DISTS with substantially lower complexity, showing that the unified model retains competitive capability for source coding. (ii) Compared with this separated counterpart, SemQAM reduces channel uses by 18.57% at matched LPIPS and outperforms the compared JSCC methods, demonstrating the benefit of joint coding.

title: Rethinking Underwater Image Enhancement: Learning through Text-Guided Degradation Curriculum
authors: Hongri Tian; Wenxue Li; Tian Ye; Sixiang Chen; Zongxian Su; Lujia Wang; Xianying Wang; Xinhu Zheng; Gang Hua; Lei Zhu
abstract: Existing paired clean-degraded datasets have advanced learning-based underwater image enhancement, but they remain either limited in scale or difficult to acquire, and still fail to adequately cover the diverse degradations encountered in real-world underwater environments. Such scarce and insufficient data ultimately restrict the generalization of underwater image enhancement models, highlighting the need for realistic and controllable degradation modeling to better capture real underwater conditions and improve enhancement robustness. To this end, we propose a unified degradation-aware training framework for the underwater image enhancement task. A Text-Conditioned Degradation Augmentation Pipeline uses a text-guided diffusion model to synthesize diverse and semantically consistent degraded samples, providing paired data to support the subsequent curriculum learning strategy. The proposed Progressive Degradation Curriculum organizes training across multiple attributes and difficulty levels to promote balanced learning, and a Transmission-Guided One-Step Diffusion Model leverages this progressive process to better address the wide range of degradation severity and restoration ambiguity in underwater images. Extensive experiments on multiple underwater benchmarks demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance. Our code and models will be released upon the publication of this work.

title: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Federated Learning (PPP-FL) for Medical Imaging
authors: Md Morshedul Islam; Hossain Shahriar; Alfredo Cuzzocrea
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that reduces transmission costs, mitigates cross-border data sharing restrictions, and enhances privacy by keeping raw data on local devices. Clients in FL systems train local models and share only updates, which are aggregated by a central server. While this setup limits direct data exposure, FL remains vulnerable to privacy attacks. Existing attack and defense strategies have largely been developed for centralized systems, and adapting them to FL introduces new challenges due to its unique architecture and training workflow. In this work, we first propose a model inversion attack on FL systems using Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGANs) in the context of large-scale medical imaging. Our method operates under realistic assumptions about the attacker's knowledge and capabilities. We then examine the effect of client-side differential privacy (DP) in mitigating privacy leakage and incorporate personalized FL to improve model performance under DP settings. Experiments on the Brain MRI ND-5 dataset show that DCGAN-based attacks can reconstruct semantically meaningful synthetic images, revealing significant risks to the privacy of training data. Applying DP reduces attack success but introduces an accuracy trade-off, which is further overcome by personalized FL at each client side. We also evaluate how different aggregation algorithms affect both attack vulnerability and defense effectiveness, underscoring the critical role of aggregation strategies. The proposed attack-and-defense framework is model-agnostic and applicable to a wide range of FL-based systems.

title: Image CL-SEC: Cross-Layer Semantic Error Correction for Image Communication
authors: Feifan Zhang; Xuelin Bai; Yirun Wang; Yuyang Du; Soung Chang Liew
abstract: Semantic error correction (SEC) uses the semantic knowledge of pretrained models to complement conventional channel decoding. By combining physical-layer decoding information with application-layer semantic predictions, cross-layer SEC (CL-SEC) has demonstrated substantial performance gains in text transmission; however, its applicability to image transmission remains largely unexplored. This paper proposes Image CL-SEC, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first extension of the CL-SEC framework to image transmission. Image CL-SEC uses channel-decoding information together with contextual predictions from a pretrained visual model to resolve residual uncertainty after forward error correction (FEC) decoding. In our implementation, images are represented as discrete visual tokens. For each token position selected for re-evaluation, the probability distribution produced by the channel decoder is combined with the distribution predicted by the visual model to identify the most likely transmitted token. The resulting decision therefore reflects both channel evidence and visual context. Experiments across multiple channel conditions show that, at low and moderate signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), Image CL-SEC improves pixel-level fidelity, perceptual similarity, and token-recovery accuracy relative to either channel decoding or visual-model inference alone. Supplementary experiments using different pretrained visual models further demonstrate that these gains are not specific to a single model.

title: Doxastic Deliberation and the Puzzles of Transparency
authors: Michael Vollmer
abstract: Abstract Doxastic deliberation about how to doxastically relate to a given proposition p is said to be transparent, in that the central deliberative question of ‘Whether to believe p?’ is equivalent to ‘Whether p?’. I discuss four challenges to this thesis based on non-evidential epistemic reasons, deliberative dilemmas, self-effecting attitudes, and permissivist pragmatism. By employing recent insights from both the theory of epistemic normativity and the literature on practical deliberation, I argue that each of these puzzles can be squared with a properly limited and constrained version of the transparency thesis. Ultimately, I show that the claim that doxastic deliberation is after settling ‘Whether p?’ can only be understood as an approximation of a sub-question of the initial normative deliberative question concerning a very specific set of attitudinal options. Nevertheless, the resulting theory retains the core motivation and upshots of the transparency thesis: one is still able to explain why the deliberative norms of doxastic deliberation appear to be, for the most part, epistemic norms.

title: Soft Power Knowledge Mapping of Nakhon Nayok Province Grounded in the Royal Duties of Her Royal Highness Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn: A Documentary Research Approach
authors: Amarin Sonsuwan
venue: Journal of Information Science Research and Practice
abstract: Purpose: This research aimed to analyze soft-power knowledge in Nakhon Nayok province and to develop a Soft Power Knowledge Map for the province, grounded in the Royal Duties of Her Royal Highness Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn. The map was designed to systematically represent the structural relationships among the key knowledge components identified in the study. Methodology: This study employed a documentary research approach. Data were drawn from 26 secondary sources, including books, textbooks, journal articles, research reports, theses, and government agency websites. The sources were selected based on criteria of relevance, credibility, currency, and data saturation. The collected data were then assessed through content analysis, categorization, and faceted knowledge structuring. Findings: Content analysis of the selected sources identified five categories of soft-power knowledge, which were synthesized into three core domains: Royal Duties, Cultural Capital, and Soft Power for the Creative Economy. These domains were further structured into a five-layer conceptual knowledge map, with storytelling functioning as the mechanism connecting and linking all the layers together. Applications of this study: The knowledge map can support soft-power policy planning, value-based tourism promotion, and sustainable knowledge management for government agencies, educational institutions, and civil-society organizations in Nakhon Nayok province. It may also serve as a reference model for other regions to consider. Furthermore, the study offers a methodological framework that may be applicable in other areas of information science.

title: Developing a multisensory smell retraining programme
authors: E. Spencer
venue: Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)
abstract: Olfactory training (OT) is a well-established intervention for enhancing smell function, but questions remain about the mechanisms underpinning its effectiveness and the features that optimise outcomes. This thesis investigates how factors such as odour pleasantness, training duration, subjective experiences, and multisensory integration contribute to OT efficacy, drawing on both quantitative and qualitative approaches. A systematic review of the OT literature revealed that improvements in olfactory function are influenced by elements such as training duration, odour selection, and adherence. However, the review also highlighted substantial methodological variation across studies, underscoring the need for more standardised and theory-driven approaches. To facilitate experimental control over odour valence in subsequent work, a stimulus set of pleasant and unpleasant odours was developed and validated through hedonic ratings, enabling precise manipulation of this dimension. Building on these foundations, a 16-week longitudinal OT study was conducted with participants with and without olfactory dysfunction who trained using a set of pleasant, unpleasant, or mixed odours. Results indicated that olfactory function improved over time regardless of odour valence, suggesting that a longer training duration may be more influential than odour pleasantness in driving improvement. To better understand the lived experience of individuals undergoing olfactory training, a qualitative study explored participants’ perceptions, and revealed four key themes: lived experiences of olfactory dysfunction; OT challenges; noticeable changes in olfactory function; and training techniques and strategies employed to facilitate training. Finally, a short-term study tested whether visual-olfactory congruency could enhance training effects over a one-week period. No significant gains were observed, indicating that brief multisensory training may be insufficient without longer engagement or additional support. Together, these findings advance understanding of how OT works, highlighting the importance of duration, baseline ability, subjective engagement, and adherence. The work contributes to the development of more effective, personalised OT interventions, particularly for use in clinical settings with individuals experiencing olfactory loss.

title: Sovereign Operating System (Sovereign OS): The Architectural Immunity Engine
authors: Eman Shafie
venue: Emirati Journal of Business Economics & Social Studies
abstract: This paper introduces Sovereign OS, a proposed deterministic framework for risk governance and structural integrity in organizational and technological systems facing increasing systemic fragility in 2026. It aims to operationalize the concepts of Invisible Assets (IA) and the Sovereign Readiness Ratio (SRR) as components of an integrated approach to organizational readiness and risk-related decision-making. The study employs a conceptual architectural approach and comparative theoretical analysis of established perspectives on risk, information theory, and systemic resilience. It examines the relationship between information integrity, internal operational constraints, and structural vulnerabilities, proposing an architecture that integrates input validation, risk assessment, and structured decision procedures. The analysis develops a conceptual framework for identifying underrecognized organizational capabilities and incorporating them into a structured assessment of operational readiness. It distinguishes information transmission from operational validity and proposes that internal structural constraints can support more systematic vulnerability assessment and risk governance. These propositions constitute a conceptual contribution rather than a claim of experimentally established performance. Sovereign OS provides a proposed architectural basis for further investigation of deterministic risk governance, with potential applications in organizational decision-making and critical infrastructure. Future empirical research should establish operational definitions for IA and SRR, evaluate the framework through reproducible simulations, and compare its performance with established risk management approaches.

title: Risk assessment of insulator contamination in thermal power plants by integrating dynamic physical priors and spatiotemporal heterogeneous graphs
authors: Zhipeng Qi; Zexi Hua; Zhongji Su; Weichen Li; Yan Li
abstract: To address the problem of predicting insulator fouling risks at thermal power plants resulting from the combined effects of various source-side facilities and meteorological conditions, we propose the Causal-STHGN model. This spatiotemporal heterogeneous graph model integrates dynamic physical priors. This paper first constructs a semantic graph of power plant entities. Source-side facility nodes are mapped to insulator monitoring points as heterogeneous nodes. Then, by integrating spatial geometric relationships, wind field directionality, source-side state characteristics, and moisture condition modulation, the model calculates dynamic physical causal priors and edge-weight priors. Furthermore, it constrains spatial dependency learning through a prior-bias graph attention mechanism. A parallel temporal structure is employed to jointly model short-term disturbances and long-term evolutionary trends. Finally, leakage current is used as a supervised proxy to calibrate the continuous risk representation, thereby evaluating the model’s ability to characterize key processes such as moisture-induced excitation and rain scouring. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method demonstrates strong overall performance across metrics including overall prediction accuracy, risk alerts, and physical consistency, and exhibits risk responses that are more in line with reality within typical event windows.

title: Typed Template Fuzzing
authors: Lu Maltsis; Dominik Winterer
abstract: Fuzzing software with complex inputs has been a longstanding challenge. Traditionally, fuzzers either programmatically encode language constraints, requiring significant engineering effort, or rely on users to declare grammars and constraints. Recent LLM-based fuzzers address these drawbacks but introduce new issues. Some use LLMs for test generation, sacrificing throughput and producing invalid inputs when the LLM makes mistakes. Others rely on language-specific parsers, static analysis, and AST manipulation libraries. We introduce Typed Template Fuzzing (TTF), a lightweight LLM-based fuzzing methodology. The key idea is to use LLMs in a preprocessing step to transform seeds into typed templates. The typed templates then enable semantically aware, mutation-based fuzzing without language-specific parsers, type checkers, or further LLM queries during fuzzing. By exploiting the correspondence between seeds and templates, TTF can moreover repair LLM mistakes. We have implemented TTF in our tool Typos, which we evaluate across 21 input languages, including C, C++, Go, Rust, SystemVerilog, Scala, and Java, as well as libraries such as PyTorch and Qiskit. In a six-month fuzzing campaign, we reported 135 bugs, 128 of which were previously unknown. Perhaps most notably, on average 96% of Typos's mutants are valid, coming close to the validity rates of domain-specific fuzzers. Our evaluation further shows Typos's benefits over the state of the art.

title: SurveyGraph: Generating Academic Surveys via Methods-Entity Knowledge Graphs
authors: Yifan Yuan; Yancheng Zhu; Zuoyu Zhang; Xiaogang Peng
abstract: Most automated survey generation systems retrieve papers as flat documents, limiting their ability to capture research structure. We present SurveyGraph, a framework built around a Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph (MEKG) encoding method-level follow-on, competition, and shared-resource relations. The graph supports core-paper discovery, retrieval, hybrid outlining, and evidence-gated narrative synthesis. We evaluate retrieval, semantic edges, citation grounding, collection coverage, and generation-stage components. In a controlled seven-method equal-budget benchmark, MEKG-anchored fusion balances recall and structural density, with an independent co-citation check. In a separate archived graph-native diagnostic, graph-aware retrieval nearly doubles recall over flat lexical baselines across eight runs (p = 0.004). A semantic evidence gate achieves AUC = 0.75. Audits of 160 generated sentences find 80.6% anchored-or-partial citation support. Human adjudication of 108 stratified semantic edges finds 68.5% supported-or-partial relations (binary-support Cohen's kappa = 0.64), with improves strongest (80.6%) and extends weakest (52.8%). A SurveyBench-facing collection probe reaches mean reference coverage of 0.521 across four topics with an eight-paper budget. Same-backend Qwen diagnostics on a 30-paper/74-relation graph show reduced organization signals when hybrid outlining is removed. Concurrent-system comparisons provide bounded context rather than matched-backend end-to-end evidence. The results position MEKG as an auditable structural layer for typed diagnostics, relation-specific filtering, and controlled survey generation. title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
authors: Hongcan Guo; Yian Zhao; Feng Wang; Shen Nie; Guoqiang Wei; Yan Zeng; Hengshuang Zhao
abstract: Hierarchical language generation separates continuous semantic modeling from discrete text realization, but its effectiveness depends on what the latent space compresses and how the discrete generator uses it. We propose Cola2, a framework that jointly studies continuous semantic compression, the balance between reconstruction and generation, and continuous-discrete co-adaptation. Cola2 dynamically segments text into semantic spans, controls the compression rate through auxiliary-loss-free negative feedback, and combines reconstruction and generation supervision to learn compact, predictive latent representations. A block-causal masked diffusion decoder is trained with clean, noisy, and dropped latent conditions, while classifier-free guidance adjusts the balance between semantic reconstruction and autonomous generation. Token-prediction gradients update the encoder through the latents, whereas Flow Matching prior learning is decoupled from representation learning by stop-gradient. During inference, generated text is re-encoded under a fixed span layout to keep the latent history consistent with the actual text context. Experiments on five downstream tasks with about 210 billion training tokens validate the core designs and show competitive, unsaturated scaling. With 346.03 billion source tokens, an unconverged checkpoint reaches a 60.10 average across eight tasks and surpasses Llama-3-8B on HellaSwag and StoryCloze despite its reported pretraining budget being over 43 times larger. These results demonstrate the potential of continuous-latent hierarchical language generation.
